other_failure_modes.name: test_statistic_leakage
other_failure_modes.description: Imputing missing values in the test set using test set statistics rather than statistics learned from the training set. This leaks test distribution information and is an invalid practice for real-world inference.

other_failure_modes.name: cv_data_leakage
other_failure_modes.description: Applying data transformations (like scaling and imputation) to the entire training set before splitting into cross-validation folds. This leaks information from the validation folds into the training folds, making the validation scores overly optimistic.

other_failure_modes.name: model_reference_bug
other_failure_modes.description: Assigning the best model during a loop using `best_model = model` without creating a copy. Because `model` is instantiated outside the loop and modified in-place, `best_model` ends up being a reference to the model trained on the final fold rather than the best fold.

other_failure_modes.name: unhandled_categorical_features
other_failure_modes.description: Passing all raw columns directly into a StandardScaler without filtering or encoding categorical/string columns. If the dataset contains any string features, this will cause a runtime error.

summary: The agent correctly frames the regression task and employs cross-validation, but the code contains severe logical bugs and instances of data leakage. Missing test values are improperly imputed using test set statistics, and training data is scaled prior to CV splitting, leaking validation data into training folds. Furthermore, an object reference bug in the CV loop ensures predictions are made using the last fold's model rather than the best one, and raw string features are dangerously passed straight to a StandardScaler.
